labels: Everything here is proposed (P) except where a name is taken from the vault or the drawn map; see 06_languages.md.

generator.determinism: Seed every draw with rng("zin-names:" + kind + ":" + entityId); entities are processed in ascending id order; the registry is global.
generator.alphabet: ^[A-Za-z]+(?:['-][A-Za-z]+)*$ (words may be separated by one space; no diacritics)

uniqueness.registry_key: lowercase letters only, no spaces, hyphens or apostrophes
collision_strategy: redraw up to 24 times with seed suffix #1..#24
add one more element or a suffix
add a house or eponym stem (people) or a directional modifier (places)
fail the build with the entity id

element_weights.note: Core elements are twice as likely; a language may boost its signature elements.

reserved_languages.note: Dwarves are Common Folk but their homeland is open [O]. No data and no generation until the owner names a homeland.
The speech of the angels. Their history is unwritten [O]. Infernal is proposed to descend from it; no data.
Mycids of the Mushroom Forest [E]; no language data until the vault describes them.
Arcanists of the Zhen Hills [E]; the hills are not placed [O].
Roka's people have no name in the vault [O]; no language.

ainic.name: Ainic family
ainic.summary: The speech of the First Men (Old Ainic) and its daughters. Aenoran is the conservative daughter and the Common Speech; Leren is clipped and northern; Dondric is blunt; Mirolic is liquid and southern; the Rite-Tongue is Old Ainic bent by the necromantic orders. What "Ainu" means is open [O].

boreal.name: Boreal family
boreal.summary: The older speech of the men of the north-west, met by Aenor's colonists in the First Age: Gunwaithic (West Lands), Coldic (Cold Lands) and Tritonic (Triton's Islands). Proposed.

eastern.name: Eastern family
eastern.summary: The speech of the river, desert and road kingdoms of the East: Noric (desert), Stabilic (trade cities) and Alerhic (river kings). Proposed.

elvish.name: Elvish family
elvish.summary: The tongues of the Great Folk elves, all descended from an Elder Elvish that nobody speaks. Sylvan, Galic and Sunhot are daughters. Galic keeps the oldest forms. Whether Gala and Sunhot are kin beyond that is open [O].

orcish.name: Orcish
orcish.summary: Orcish and the goblin cant, with a shared Horde Cant used between holds.

isolates.name: Isolates
isolates.summary: Languages with no known relative: Orran (older than Ainic), Yonic (the southern islands), Trollish, the Giants' Speech, Yeti Speech, the Long Speech of the ents, and Infernal (proposed to descend from the lost Choral tongue).

aenoran.name: Aenoran
aenoran.summary: The Common Speech of Erdae: the language of Parim, of the Concord, of the charts and of trade from the North Lands to the East. Every other tongue of men borrows its titles and its road-words.

script.name: Common hand
script.feel: a running script of joined letters, written with a reed pen on paper; the Houses of the First Light teach it to every child

sound.consonants: p t k b d g f v s z h m n l r j
sound.codas: l r n m s t d
sound.orthography: Plain Latin letters. z appears only between vowels or as the sound of s between vowels (Herez). th and w are lost.
signature: ends in e after a consonant

morphology.notes: Genitive by -an after the possessor. Chart names add -dor to a people or a ruler.

sound_laws: p t k > b d g between vowels

house.notes: Surnames are place-names with a suffix. Houses of long standing take the Ainic -dil in formal records.

patronymic.rule: Commoners may add -sen to the father's given name: used on the frontier and in the dominions, not in Parim.

person.notes: The ruling house uses Ainic royal endings. The common stock uses short names ending in -an, -on or -ec.

established_names.name: Aenor
established_names.reading: Open [O]. "Aen" + "-or" (realm) is a possible reading; whether Aenor is named for Aen stays open.

established_names.name: Parim
established_names.reading: Aenoran par "lake" + -im "place of": the lake-place.

established_names.name: Selen
established_names.reading: Aenoran sel "forest" + -en "dwellers": the forest-dwellers.

established_names.name: Hunhun
established_names.reading: Aenoran rider dialect: hun "horse" said twice, "many horses".

ainic.name: Old Ainic
ainic.summary: The speech of the First Men. Nobody speaks it now. It is kept for royal names, law, temple rites and the oldest place names.
speakers: every dynasty that claims descent from Aen

script.name: Aenic hand
script.feel: ring-and-stroke letters, one ring per consonant and a stroke for each vowel; carved in stone, written on wax and vellum; read left to right

sound.consonants: p t k b d g f v s h m n l r w y th
sound.syllable: (C)(C)V(C); stop plus r is the only onset cluster
sound.codas: l r n s m th (st and rd in a few learned words)
sound.orthography: Plain Latin letters. Long vowels are not marked. th is one sound.
rules: every name ends in a vowel or l r n s m th
names of kings end in -dil, -or, -an or -ath

morphology.notes: No article. Plural by -im. Genitive by -or after the possessor. The patronymic -dil follows the father or mother.

sound_laws: proto-language: stems as written in the family table

patronymic.rule: Given name + dil + the parent's name: Eindil is "child of Ein" (P reading).

person.notes: Regnal names are built from a stem and a royal ending and always take a number in Aenoran use.

dondric.name: Dondric
dondric.summary: The blunt tongue of the Dondor Brutes. It is Old Ainic worn down by centuries of living beside orc holds: voiced stops, a flat vowel stock and many words taken from Orcish.

script.name: Notched marks
script.feel: tally-like notches on staves, with a thin Common hand used by clerks

sound.consonants: b d g z m n l r w y
sound.codas: any; final b d g are voiceless k t p
sound.orthography: Plain letters. oa is a broad a. No p, t or k at the start of a word.
rules: stops are voiced at the start and inside
no th, no f, no h

morphology.notes: No article. The tribal plural is -ung (Dondung "Dondor folk"). Orcish loans keep their gh as g.

sound_laws: ae > oa, ai > ua, ei > ui, au > o
p t k > b d g
final vowel lost in words of two or more syllables

house.notes: A brute carries his clan: Gulung. Chiefs add the hold name.

patronymic.rule: Son of is -ug after the father (Dunug).

person.notes: Dondor kings are chosen by the clan-moot from the strongest line.

established_names.name: Dondor
established_names.reading: Dondric don "hold" + dor "land": the hold-land.

leren.name: Leren
leren.summary: The sea-speech of the North Lands: clipped, with long vowels and hard endings. It dropped the soft final vowels of Old Ainic and borrowed its sailing words from the Seaspeech of the northern coasts.

script.name: Leren strokes
script.feel: angular letters cut into driftwood and slate; a cursive form for ledgers

sound.consonants: p t k b d g f v s h m n l r ng
sound.vowels: a e i o u aa ee oo
sound.codas: any single consonant; rk rn rd lk nd ng sk st
sound.orthography: Long vowels are doubled. w is written v. Final b d g are written p t k.
rules: no word ends in an open vowel except -o and -a in loan names

morphology.notes: The definite article is a suffix -en (Sonargur-en "the Sonargur"), used only in speech. Compounds are closed. Genitive by -s.

sound_laws: ae > ee, ai > ei, au > ou
final vowel lost in words of two or more syllables
final b d g > p t k

house.notes: A Leren surname is a farm or bay name. Nobles add -kov or -vik; commoners use -son after the father.

patronymic.rule: Given name + father's name + son (male) or dot (female).

person.notes: A king takes a number: Ferlin III. A ruler of the union adds both crowns: of Lerendor and Lerenwaith.

established_names.name: Lerendor
established_names.reading: Leren + chart -dor "land": the Leren land. Lerenwaith is the Leren shore.

mirolic.name: Mirolic
mirolic.summary: The liquid speech of the lake-country of the Dead Lands: a southern daughter of Old Ainic that lost p-less roots, k and s. It sounds of l, m, n and r.

script.name: Common hand with warden marks
script.feel: the Common hand, with a signal alphabet of knotted cords used by the pass watch

sound.consonants: p b d g f v h m n l r
sound.codas: l m n r
sound.orthography: Plain letters. The language has no k, no s and no th: the letters never appear.
rules: l, m, n and r make up half the letters

morphology.notes: The suffix -on makes a place from a people or a feature. Plural by -en.

house.notes: A warden is "of" a lake, a pass or a hold: Maeric of Miherta.

patronymic.rule: Rarely used.

person.notes: The ruling office is elective; the title is the same for both sexes.

established_names.name: Mirolon
established_names.reading: Mirolic mir (an old root, "lake") + ol "watch" + -on: the lake-watch.

grave_rite.name: Rite-Tongue
grave_rite.summary: The ritual speech of the necromantic orders of Volgan and, in memory, of Elzon's Order. It is Old Ainic funeral formulas bent into a cold, fixed form. The dead do not speak it: they speak the tongue they spoke alive. Offices, binding-names and gate-names are written in it.
speakers: officers of the grave hosts (titles only)

script.name: Ash script
script.feel: thin straight strokes burned or scratched into bone, slate and lead tablets; no curves

sound.consonants: p t q b d g f v x h m n l r
sound.codas: l r n m x s
sound.orthography: x stands for the hiss of old s; q for old k. Names are never given a double letter.
rules: no th, no k, no s: x and q replace them

morphology.notes: Offices are written head first: the thing, then its place or number. A binding-name ends in -x.

patronymic.rule: The dead carry no father's name.

person.notes: A name remembered from life shrinks to a binding-name of one or two syllables.

orran.name: Orran
orran.summary: The speech of the kingdoms Aen defeated: a language older than Ainic that survives in the Bloody Forest, among the Cursed Lands and under the river-names of the Middle Lands. It has no known relative.

script.name: Knot-script
script.feel: strings of knots and notched sticks; the forest tribes write nothing on paper and bar it

sound.consonants: p b t d k g tz z kh m n l r rr
sound.codas: k r z n l tz
sound.orthography: tz and kh are single sounds. rr is a rolled r. No f, no v, no h by itself, no w, no y.
rules: rr and tz are the marks of the language

morphology.notes: The adjective follows the noun. A place is marked by -ar. The plural is -ak.

house.notes: A person belongs to a tree or beast-clan: Urnakak "the Wolf-folk".

patronymic.rule: Mother-line: Given name + mother's name + en. Orran descent runs through mothers.

person.notes: Chiefs are women or men chosen by the clan-mothers.

alerhic.name: Alerhic
alerhic.summary: The court tongue of the river kingdoms of the East: stately, with rh and th, and endings in -ia, -is and -oth. It was the language of scribes and priests long before the caravan roads.

script.name: Reed letters
script.feel: rounded letters pressed into clay and written in ink on papyrus-like reed sheets; court seals are cut in stone

sound.consonants: p t k b d g f s th ch m n l r rh w y z
sound.codas: n r s th l
sound.orthography: rh is a rolled, breathy r at the start of a word. th is one sound. ch is the Scottish sound.

morphology.notes: Genitive by -on after the possessor (Alerh-on-ia). Kingdoms end in -ia.

house.notes: River dynasties take a surname ending -ides; temple families -os.

patronymic.rule: Son of is -ides after the father's stem.

person.notes: Kings take a number and the name of the river that crowned them.

established_names.name: Mora
established_names.reading: Alerhic mora, "field".

established_names.name: Alerhia
established_names.reading: Alerhic alerh (the river-people) + -ia "kingdom".

coldic.name: Coldic
coldic.summary: The hard speech of the Cold Lands: v and z, a short ae, and endings that close on r, k or m. It is the oldest living tongue of men in the north-west and has borrowed only road-words from Aenoran.

script.name: Frost-runes
script.feel: upright runes cut with a knife into bone, birch bark and ice-stone; a pen form for the chanceries of Fandanar

sound.consonants: p t k b d g f v s z h m n l r
sound.codas: r k m n d t l
sound.orthography: Plain letters. w is written v. The Common chart spelling keeps w in old names (Windwaith).
rules: v for w; z for s between vowels

morphology.notes: No article. The genitive is -s after a vowel. Compounds are closed.

sound_laws: final vowel lost in words of two or more syllables

house.notes: A surname is a hearth-line: stem + -ing for old lines, -air for coast families.

patronymic.rule: Given name + father's name + son or dot, used by clanfolk who have no surname.

person.notes: The Winter Crown passes in the female line as often as the male.

established_names.name: Coldor
established_names.reading: Coldic kold "ice" + chart -dor "land": the ice-land.

established_names.name: Isengard
established_names.reading: Coldic isen "iron" + gard "stronghold".

established_names.name: Windwaith
established_names.reading: Coldic vind "wind" + vait "shore" (native Vindvait; the chart spelling keeps w).

gunwaithic.name: Gunwaithic
gunwaithic.summary: The clan-speech of the West Lands, the tongue that Aenor's colonists met on the western shores. It puts the noun first and the adjective after, and it has gw, ch and a soft th. Chart forms spell its names with Aenoran endings.

script.name: Clan-ogham
script.feel: notches along the edge of a stave or a standing stone; guildmen use the Common hand for contracts

sound.consonants: p t c k b d g gw w f v s h ch m n l r
sound.vowels: a e i o u y
sound.codas: r l n th d t
sound.orthography: gw is one sound; ch is the sound in Scottish loch; y is a vowel as in "myth".
rules: noun first, adjective after, joined by a hyphen
no z, no x, no j

morphology.notes: Descriptive names are head-first and hyphenated (Chalwe-Gwit, "White Hall"). Eponym names are closed. Chart forms add -on or -in to a stem.

sound_laws: final -a lost in words of two or more syllables
k before e i y > c

house.notes: A clan name is a stem plus -wyn ("folk of"). A warden of Girdon takes the river or ford he guards.

patronymic.rule: Given + ap + father's name (Tarlic ap Dat). Women use ach.

person.notes: A clan king is acclaimed at a standing stone and bound by the Lawspeaker.

established_names.name: Gunwaith
established_names.reading: Gunwaithic gun- (a clan name, open) + waith "shore".

noric.name: Noric
noric.summary: The desert speech of the camel kings: long vowels, q and kh, and words that end on a hard stop. It is the tongue of wells, caravans and sworn oaths.
speakers: desert kingdoms of the South Lands

script.name: Sand script
script.feel: flowing letters joined along a baseline, written right to left with a reed; caravan marks are knotted on cords

sound.consonants: b d g h k kh q m n l r s sh t w y z
sound.vowels: a e i o u aa ii uu oo
sound.codas: any single consonant; rq rb rz lk
sound.orthography: Long vowels are doubled. q is a throat k. kh is the sound in loch.
rules: short words: one or two syllables
q, kh and doubled vowels mark the tongue

morphology.notes: Construct state: the thing comes first and the quality follows, joined by a hyphen (Wahe-Rakh, "Red Oasis"). A people is named with -ud.

sound_laws: final vowel lost in words of two or more syllables
a u i o doubled before a final consonant in one-syllable roots

house.notes: A tribe-name ending -i is carried by every member: Kersi of the Kers.

patronymic.rule: Given + ben (son) or bat (daughter) + father's name; used by every free man of the sand.

person.notes: The king of Noris is the war-leader of the tribes, chosen by the well-lords from one line.

established_names.name: Noris
established_names.reading: Noric nuuv "new" + -is "country": the New Country of the tribes who crossed the plain.

stabilic.name: Stabilic
stabilic.summary: The merchant tongue of the southern trade cities: it drops the vowel after a first stop, ends every word in -o, -a or -io, and has the clusters pl, pr, st and tr. It is the language of contracts and scales.

script.name: Ledger hand
script.feel: upright letters with long tails, written in ink on rolled paper; seals are cut in bronze

sound.consonants: p t c ch b d g f v s z m n l r
sound.codas: n r s l
sound.orthography: c is always hard, ch is soft, as in "church".
rules: clusters pl pr tr st cr bl are allowed at the start
no kh, no q, no sh

morphology.notes: Descriptive names put the quality last and join with -o- (Portocairo). The merchant's mark follows the town (Postondoroth-Gold).

sound_laws: kh > c, q > c, sh > s, k > c
vowel lost between an initial stop and r

house.notes: A merchant house takes the name of its founding ledger: stem + -o. Houses write their mark before the name in contracts.

patronymic.rule: Rare: Given + di + father's given name.

person.notes: The prince of Stabilo is first among the factors, chosen by the bench of houses.

established_names.name: Postondoroth
established_names.reading: Stabilic porto "harbour" + -on "great" + dor + oth "high": the great high harbour-land.

established_names.name: Stabilo
established_names.reading: Stabilic stab- (a house name) + -ilo, a diminutive of respect.

tritonic.name: Tritonic
tritonic.summary: The island speech of the Pupor Ocean: an open tongue that gives every word a vowel ending and loves the sound ai. Its sailors named the reefs, tides and straits that every chart now carries.

script.name: Chart-hand
script.feel: small joined letters written with fine pens on sea-charts; islanders also tally with knotted cords

sound.consonants: p t k b d g f v s h m n l r
sound.codas: s n l
sound.orthography: Plain letters. ai is always two sounds said fast.
rules: almost every name ends in a vowel or -os -on -an
ai and ei are the marks of the tongue

morphology.notes: The island is named for its first harbour. Plural by -ai.

house.notes: A chart-house keeps its first reef or harbour as a surname.

patronymic.rule: Rare: Given + father's name + idas.

person.notes: Most island lords are elected Speakers; the few kings (Nondondor) are sea-kings.

yonic.name: Yonic
yonic.summary: The island speech of the Islands of the South: open syllables, y and w glides, and a final n or ng. Names are repeated for the plural (Yongyong "many Yong"). Its sailors share a trade vocabulary with the eastern Sunhot isles.

script.name: Wave-tally
script.feel: rows of short strokes and loops cut on bamboo-like canes and shell; a Common hand is taught in the harbour towns

sound.consonants: p t k b d g m n ng l r s h w y j
sound.codas: n ng
sound.orthography: ng is one sound. y and w are glides. Every syllable has one vowel.
rules: open syllables, closing only on n or ng

morphology.notes: The head comes first and the quality second, as separate words (Kamu Ronga, "Red Isle"). A single island takes a bare root. Plural by repetition.

patronymic.rule: Given + nau + the name of the island or the elder who raised the child.

person.notes: An elder speaks for a harbour and its fields. The title does not separate the sexes.

galic.name: Galic
galic.summary: The court language of the Gala elves. It keeps the oldest forms of Elder Elvish: long vowels split into ea and ie, final -ien, and names written as two stately words. Whether it is kin to Sunhot beyond the common Elder root is left open.
speakers: Gala, North Gala and the Gala Elves

script.name: Sun-hand
script.feel: tall letters with a bar across the top like a horizon, painted in gold ink on pale vellum

sound.consonants: p t c b d g f v s m n l r w y
sound.codas: n l r t s
sound.orthography: Plain letters; c is always hard. There is no th and no h at the start of a word.
rules: descriptive names are two words, noun first

morphology.notes: The noun comes first, then the quality: Corin Aila "Bright Fort". Place names with a suffix are one word.

house.notes: A Gala lord is "of" his seat. There are no surnames.

patronymic.rule: None; the Gala remember lineages by the Mirror's keepers and not by names.

person.notes: Kings hold the crown for as long as they will. Lorien's name is unique and is never given.

sunhot.name: Sunhot
sunhot.summary: The warm, open speech of the Sunhot elves. It turns th into s, k into h and a final n or m into ng, so that names ring: Hengyang, Poyang. Two dialects exist, Western Sanctuary and Eastern Isle.
speakers: Sunhot elves of the Lands of Light

script.name: Noon-script
script.feel: round open letters like rising suns, written with a wide brush in bright mineral inks on silk and on the doors of sanctuaries

sound.consonants: p t k h b d g s m n ng l y w v
sound.codas: n ng l s
sound.orthography: ng is one sound and may close a word. y is a glide. r is written l between vowels.

morphology.notes: Noun first, quality second, as separate words (Yeni Alang, "High Valley"). Single-word names take a bare root.

house.notes: A person is "of" a sanctuary. There are no surnames.

patronymic.rule: None.

person.notes: The largest realm is led by a Radiant Speaker, chosen by the sanctuaries. Elders are never called king.

sylvan.name: Sylvan
sylvan.summary: The flowing speech of the elves of the Magical Lands. It lenites its inner consonants, ends many words in -iel and puts a soft v where Elder Elvish had w. The elected houses debate in it and write their laws in it.
speakers: Magical Forest and its council houses

script.name: Leaf-script
script.feel: flowing joined letters drawn with a brush, each word a single curved line; carved on bark-paper and on the stone of the Great Wall's elven gates

sound.consonants: p t th k h b d g f v s m n l r w y
sound.codas: l n r th s
sound.orthography: Plain letters; th is one sound. iel is three sounds said as one.
rules: between vowels t becomes th and k becomes h
no hard clusters of three consonants

morphology.notes: Genitive by -in after the possessor. House names are used as a prefix to the person (Velakorin Lusiel in the council; Lusiel Velakorin in speech).

sound_laws: t > th and k > h between vowels

house.notes: A house is named for its founder's stem plus an ending; the elected speaker keeps her house name for life.

patronymic.rule: Rare; elves count by house.

person.notes: The first among the houses is called First Speaker and is elected for a term of years that can be long.

gigantic.name: Giants' Speech
gigantic.summary: The slow, deep speech of the giants: long vowels, r, n and m, and words that take a breath to say. Hiloron's hill-giants and Titanos's ice-giants speak two dialects that differ in their vowels and in the Titanos love of cold words.

script.name: Cairn-tally
script.feel: single great strokes scratched on standing stones; each stone carries one word

sound.consonants: b d g h m n r t l s p
sound.vowels: a e i o u aa oo uu
sound.codas: n m r
sound.orthography: Long vowels are doubled. There is no sharp sound: no k, no z, no x.
rules: three or four syllables are normal for a place

morphology.notes: The Titanos dialect shortens final -un to -u and prefers cold words. Hiloron keeps -un.

patronymic.rule: None; a giant gives his steps instead.

person.notes: Giants live long and name late: a child is called "Small" for forty years.

established_names.name: Hiloron
established_names.reading: Aenoran hil "hill" + Giants' oron "giant": the giants' hill.

established_names.name: Titanos
established_names.reading: Giants' Speech tiran "white, cold" with the Titanos plural -os.

goblin.name: Goblin Cant
goblin.summary: The quick cant of the goblin warrens: a high, clipped speech of short words, doubled k and t, and many words for tunnels, traps and light. Goblins of different warrens understand each other; orcs mostly do not try.
speakers: Goblin Warrens (a minor people of some orc holds)

script.name: Scratch-tally
script.feel: quick scratches on tunnel walls, with arrows for direction; nothing is ever written to be kept

sound.consonants: b d g k kk p r s sk sn t tt z w l
sound.codas: k t x p b
sound.orthography: kk and tt are doubled for sharpness. i is the favoured vowel.
rules: i and k carry the tongue

morphology.notes: Plural by -s in Cant (a loan from the Common Speech).

patronymic.rule: None; goblins know their warren, not their parents.

person.notes: A warren obeys its loudest and cleverest.

infernal.name: Infernal
infernal.summary: The harsh tongue of the demons of the Nether: z, v, th, kh and rolled rr, with endings in -ath and -azel. It is said to be the old Choral speech of the angels, bent and hardened (the corruption account is proposed, and the angels' own tongue is not written).
speakers: Netherborn of Demon, Dolon and Nezer

script.name: Cinder-script
script.feel: angular sharp glyphs burned into black stone with a hot point; the demons of Dolon also write in salt

sound.consonants: b d g z v th kh zh s sh k t r rr n m l
sound.codas: th k r z l m n
sound.orthography: kh and zh are single sounds. rr is rolled hard. th is as in "thin".
rules: z, kh and th are the marks of the tongue

morphology.notes: The thing first, the quality after, joined by a hyphen (Vorath-Nazur, "Dark Gate"). A lord is named with his house as a suffix: -ath.

patronymic.rule: None; demons name their pact.

person.notes: A lord of the Nether takes a name of two beats and a pact-name that only the pact knows.

longspeech.name: the Long Speech
longspeech.summary: The language of the ents: slow, doubled and deep. A word can take a minute to say and a name is a short song. Ents rarely say anything twice, and men learn only a few words of it.

script.name: Ring-marks
script.feel: concentric rings carved into the bark of old trees; each ring is a year and a syllable

sound.consonants: g h l m n r s b d
sound.vowels: a o u e i aa oo
sound.codas: m n r l ll nn rr mm
sound.orthography: Doubled letters are held a long time. There is no k, no t and no p.
rules: no k, no t, no p
a place is three or four syllables

morphology.notes: No article. A name is built from two or three roots said slowly.

patronymic.rule: None; ents name their groves.

person.notes: The Eldest is the one who has said the fewest words in the year.

established_names.name: Kilinti
established_names.reading: Long Speech kilin "grove" + -ti, a plural of respect (P).

orcish.name: Orcish
orcish.summary: The war-speech of the orc holds: closed syllables, hard stops and the sounds gh, kh, zg and zh. Holds differ: the Volcano Clans of Goldoroth speak slow and deep, the Iron Clans clipped and fast, the Wild Holds with many loan-words. A Horde Cant of mixed words is used between holds and in armies.

script.name: Scar-marks
script.feel: straight scratches cut with a blade into bone, iron and leather; a tally of kills and debts; clerks of the larger holds use the Common hand

sound.consonants: b d g gh k kh m n r s sh t z zg zh l w
sound.codas: g k r z gh sh th rk rg zg lk
sound.orthography: gh and kh are throat sounds; zg and zh are single sounds; there is no e.
rules: a name of one or two syllables

morphology.notes: No article. Plural by -ash. Compounds are closed and stress the first part.

house.notes: A clan is a totem-word plus -gul. A warrior may add the name of his hold.

patronymic.rule: Mother-line is counted: Given + ug + the mother's name is a boast, not a rule.

person.notes: A chief holds his hold until a stronger challenger breaks him in the ring. The Warking of Goldoroth is acclaimed by the clan chiefs.

established_names.name: Goldoroth
established_names.reading: Chart form gold + dor + oth "high": the high gold-land. The orcs' own name is Gruzgoroth (P).

trollish.name: Trollish
trollish.summary: The slow speech of the troll tribes: few words, long vowels and heavy closed syllables. Trolls name things for their weight. A name is one or two beats and is said low.

script.name: Stone-heaps
script.feel: trolls write nothing; they pile stones in patterns at tribe borders

sound.consonants: b g m n r t d k w l
sound.codas: m n g k rr mm gg
sound.orthography: Long vowels are doubled. Doubled consonants are held.
rules: a name never has more than two syllables

morphology.notes: Plural by repeating the last syllable (Grumum "many Grum").

patronymic.rule: None.

person.notes: The oldest troll who has not been beaten leads the tribe.

yetic.name: Yeti Speech
yetic.summary: The sung speech of the yeti: soft h and m, long u and a, and calls that rise and fall. Yeti hum their names as much as say them.

script.name: Hum-marks
script.feel: none in the human sense: clan marks scratched on ice and a counting of pebbles; men write yeti words in the Common hand

sound.consonants: h hh m n g gh r l y w s
sound.vowels: u a o i uu aa
sound.codas: m n l h gh
sound.orthography: hh is a breath. gh is soft, in the throat. Doubled vowels are held.
rules: no p, no t, no k, no b, no d
every name has an h or an m

morphology.notes: Plural by lengthening the vowel.

patronymic.rule: None; a yeti is known by the song of his clan.

person.notes: The eldest sings the clan's names at the winter gathering.
